findings.claim: the Foundling Hospital becomes a place of salvation for Aaron (Toby)
findings.truth: Aaron and Toby are two different boys. Aaron is Alexander and Melissa's illegitimate son, saved by Meshak and named Aaron by the Coram Hospital staff. Toby is an African boy rescued from a slave ship who becomes Aaron's closest friend. The same lesson later calls Toby 'a Black child at the Foundling Hospital', contradicting itself.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Coram Boy (play): 'two orphans: Toby, saved from an African slave ship; and Aaron, the deserted son of the heir to an estate.' eNotes: 'The staff at Coram name the child Aaron.'

findings.claim: the Foundling Hospital, which opened in 1739 in Bloomsbury, London
findings.truth: The royal charter was granted in 1739. The Hospital first admitted children on 25 March 1741, into a temporary house in Hatton Garden. The Bloomsbury building (Lamb's Conduit Fields) opened from October 1745.
findings.evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foundling_Hospital - charter 1739; first admissions 25 March 1741 Hatton Garden; western wing Lamb's Conduit Field finished October 1745.

findings.claim: In which year and location did the Foundling Hospital open? - '1739, in Bloomsbury, London.'
findings.truth: 1741, in Hatton Garden, London.

findings.claim: Which award did the 2005 National Theatre stage adaptation of Coram Boy win? - 'The Olivier Award for Best New Play.'
findings.truth: The adaptation did not win Best New Play. It received four Olivier nominations in 2006 (Best New Play, Best Director, Best Sound Design, Best Performance in a Supporting Role). The lesson's own body text says 'four Olivier Award nominations', so the card contradicts the article beside it.
findings.evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coram_Boy - awards section lists nominations only; the sole win recorded is a Theatre World Award for Xanthe Elbrick, 2007.

findings.claim: All 42 practice questions (6 in each of the 7 lessons) carry the mark scheme 'AO1 (up to 20 marks) / AO3 (up to 12 marks) / AO4 (up to 8 marks)'. Thirteen of them instead carry 'AO1 (up to 10 marks) / AO3 (up to 6 marks) / AO4 (up to 4 marks)' with a 1-20 band ladder, while still labelled '40 marks'. Several ladders name two different mark ranges 'Top band' (for example 33-40 and 17-24 in the same scheme).
findings.truth: On the Edexcel post-1914 British play or novel essay the raw marks are AO1 16 + AO3 16 + AO4 8 = 40. AO2 is not assessed. A 20-mark ladder under a 40-mark heading is the wrong board's shape and would mislead a student about how much each objective is worth.
findings.evidence: specs/edexcel/english-literature-1ET0.md - Overview of assessment: 'Section B - Post-1914 British play or novel: students answer ONE essay question from a choice of two'; 'Assessment Objectives covered are AO1, AO3 and AO4.' Raw mark distribution table (Questions 7 to 30): AO1 16, AO3 16, AO4 8, total 40.

findings.claim: Every key event in Parts 2 and 3 has its origin here
findings.truth: Coram Boy is a novel in two parts: Part One (1741) and Part Two (1750), with a prologue and an epilogue. There is no Part 3.
findings.evidence: BBC Bitesize plot overview: 'Coram Boy is a novel in two parts. Part One is set in 1741. Part Two is set in 1750.' Chase Terrace Academy knowledge organiser: 'Part One - 1741 ... Part Two - 1750'.

findings.claim: The baby Meshak saved is now a boy called Toby - later known as Aaron ... Alongside him is his closest friend, also called Toby, a Black child.
findings.truth: Aaron was never called Toby. The Coram Hospital staff named him Aaron. Toby is the separate African boy rescued from a slave ship. The lesson invents a name-change and then places two Tobys in the same sentence.

findings.claim: Toby: 'The name given to Alexander and Melissa's son at the Foundling Hospital, later revealed to be called Aaron.'
findings.truth: Toby is an African boy rescued from a slave ship who grows up at the Foundling Hospital and becomes Aaron's closest friend. The same wrong text sat in the content_html data-def attribute.

findings.claim: 'What name is Aaron given at the Foundling Hospital?' - correct answer marked as 'Toby'.
findings.truth: The check rewards the fabrication and would mark the true answer (Aaron) wrong. The question has been rewritten so the same option index ('Toby') is the correct answer to a true question about the boy rescued from a slave ship.

findings.claim: 'What was Aaron's name at the Foundling Hospital?' - 'Toby.'
findings.truth: Aaron was named Aaron by the Hospital staff.

findings.claim: 'Who is Aaron's closest foundling friend, also named Toby?'
findings.truth: 'Also named Toby' repeats the invented claim that Aaron was called Toby.

findings.claim: Part 2 centres on Aaron (Toby) growing up at the Foundling Hospital
findings.truth: Aaron and Toby are different boys.

findings.claim: description = 'TEST UPDATE'
findings.truth: A leftover test string is live on a lesson card. It is also 11 characters, below the 60-character floor the house validator enforces.

findings.claim: 'Part 3: Discovery and Resolution'; 'The central revelation of Part 3'; 'how Part 3 resolves the novel's conflicts'; plus two practice questions, one knowledge check and three flashcards that refer to Part 3.
findings.truth: The novel has two parts only. Every 'Part 3' reference has been changed to a neutral description of the closing chapters.

findings.claim: 'Meshak makes the ultimate _____ to protect Aaron from Otis, choosing to save the child even at the cost of his own life.'
findings.truth: Meshak does not die saving Aaron. He stays on the boat, returns to England, and his peaceful death is described in the epilogue. The character killed in the rescue is Thomas Ledbury. The lesson's own body text already states this, so the knowledge check contradicts the article beside it.
findings.evidence: BBC Bitesize plot overview: 'Meshak stays on the boat. He eventually returns to England and his life and peaceful death are described in the epilogue.' Chase Terrace Academy knowledge organiser: 'Meshak's peaceful death is described in the epilogue.'

findings.claim: 'Aaron is reunited with his parents, but _____ is dead' - correct answer marked as 'Meshak'.
findings.truth: Thomas Ledbury is the character who is dead at the end. The option text has been changed; the correct index is unchanged.

findings.claim: Matching item 'Meshak's death' paired with 'Proves the least valued character is the most morally courageous'.
findings.truth: The pairing rests on Meshak dying in the rescue. Changed to 'Meshak saving baby Aaron', which the same right-hand text fits.

findings.claim: discuss ... what is lost (Meshak's life, Aaron's foundling years, the other buried babies)
findings.truth: Meshak's life is not lost in the rescue. Thomas Ledbury's is.

findings.claim: Heading 'Aaron (Toby)' and 'Aaron grows up at the Foundling Hospital under the name Toby'
findings.truth: Aaron and Toby are different boys.

findings.claim: his death is one of the novel's most shocking moments and's storylines together.
findings.truth: The sentence is corrupt: a clause has been spliced out and left the fragment 'and's storylines together'. A student reading the lesson meets broken text.
findings.evidence: Raw lesson 5 content_html, narration block n13.

findings.claim: 'What name does Aaron grow up under at the Foundling Hospital?' - 'Toby - he is unaware of his true parentage...'
findings.truth: Aaron grows up under the name Aaron.

findings.claim: 'Who does Meshak ultimately sacrifice his life to protect?' - 'Aaron - his final act of moral courage...'
findings.truth: Meshak does not give his life for Aaron. He saves the newborn by hiding him instead of burying him, then dies peacefully in the epilogue years later.

findings.claim: Melissa is 'the daughter of a local family' (also in lesson 2 content_html data-def, lesson 2 glossary and a lesson 2 flashcard).
findings.truth: Melissa is Mrs Milcote's daughter. Mrs Milcote is the Ashbrook children's governess and lives in the household. Melissa is therefore of the servant class, which is exactly why a marriage to Alexander would have been unthinkable - the context point the lesson is trying to make.
findings.evidence: BBC Bitesize characters page: 'Melissa is Mrs Milcote's daughter (the Ashbrook children's governess).' Chase Terrace Academy knowledge organiser: 'Melissa - is the daughter of the Ashbrook children's governess ... would still have been regarded as part of the servant class.'

findings.claim: 'Part 3 brings these timelines together'; 'the resolution in Part 3'; conclusion 'separate until Part 3'; two flashcards referring to Part 3.
findings.truth: The novel has two parts.

findings.claim: 'A dual timeline - parallel plots converging in Part 3'; 'What sustained form of irony runs from Part 1 to Part 3?'
findings.truth: There is no Part 3.

findings.claim: 'Which Assessment Objectives are tested in Section B of the Edexcel English Literature Component 1 exam?'
findings.truth: 'Component 1' is a banned spec code. The house validator (scripts/_validate_content_json.py, pattern \bComponent\s+[0-9][a-z]?\b) rejects the whole unit on it. The answer index is correct (AO1, AO3 and AO4) and is unchanged.
findings.evidence: scripts/_validate_content_json.py BANNED_PATTERNS; CHECK_PROMPT.md banned strings list.

findings.claim: Meshak sacrifices himself for a child
findings.truth: Meshak risks everything to save Aaron but survives; he dies peacefully in the epilogue.

findings.claim: 'Who sacrifices himself to save Aaron from Otis?' - 'Meshak.'
findings.truth: Thomas Ledbury is the character killed during the rescue of Aaron and Toby.

findings.claim: Lesson 4 is titled 'Part 3: Discovery & Resolution'.
findings.truth: The novel has two parts, so no lesson should be titled Part 3. The heading, body text, questions and cards inside the lesson are fixed by F14, but the lesson title is not one of the fields the edit schema covers. It needs a manual retitle, for example 'Discovery & Resolution'. Note this also leaves the unit with lessons 3 and 4 both covering Part 2 of the novel, which is fine as a teaching split but should be reflected in the titles.

findings.claim: 'dual timeline: A narrative structure where two separate time periods are presented in parallel, converging towards a climactic moment.'
findings.truth: Coram Boy is sequential, not parallel: Part One runs through 1741, then the narrative jumps nine years to 1750. Nothing is presented in parallel. 'Dual timeline' is a common classroom label for a novel with a large time jump, so the term itself is defensible, but 'presented in parallel' is not. Correcting it means rewriting the data-def in content_html, the glossary entry, one knowledge check and three flashcards, so it is left for a decision rather than edited.
findings.evidence: As F6. Lesson 6 itself says 'Part 1 is set in 1741 ... Part 2 jumps forward to 1750', which contradicts 'in parallel'.

findings.claim: Thomas Ledbury 'is shot and killed by Gaddarn (Otis)' (also lesson 5 and a lesson 4 flashcard).
findings.truth: Sources agree Thomas dies in the rescue but disagree on the weapon. SuperSummary says he is shot; a widely used school knowledge organiser says he dies on Otis's sword. Not edited - the death itself is not in doubt, and no source was found that settles the weapon.
findings.evidence: SuperSummary Coram Boy summary: 'Alexander's childhood friend, Thomas, is shot and killed during the rescue effort.' Chase Terrace Academy knowledge organiser: 'giving up his life to save his friend from Otis's sword.'

findings.claim: 'Alexander eventually defies Sir William to study under Handel in London' (also a lesson 5 flashcard and lesson 2).
findings.truth: Alexander leaves home to pursue music in London and is a successful musician by Part Two, but no source found states that Handel taught him. The claim may be an invention. Not edited without proof.
findings.evidence: Chase Terrace Academy knowledge organiser Part Two summary makes Alexander a tutor to Aaron and a singer at Gaddarn's, with no mention of Handel tutoring him.

summary: Every one of the 7 lessons is affected. The unit invents a third part of the novel (there are two, 1741 and 1750), invents a name-change in which Aaron grows up as 'Toby' (Toby is a separate African boy rescued from a slave ship), and in the practice material still has Meshak dying to save Aaron when the lesson body text has already been corrected to say Thomas Ledbury dies and Meshak dies peacefully in the epilogue. All 42 practice questions carry the wrong assessment-objective split for the Edexcel post-1914 essay (AO1 16 + AO3 16 + AO4 8 = 40, not AO1 20 / AO3 12), and 13 of them run a 1-20 band ladder under a 40-mark label. Lesson 4's live description is the string 'TEST UPDATE', lesson 5 contains a corrupt half-sentence, and one knowledge check carries the banned code 'Component 1' which would fail the whole unit in the house validator.
